topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic covers the opening framing and the key learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer evolution.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations, Darwinian selection, and epigenetic alterations drive clonal fitness and tumor initiation.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell properties, differentiation hierarchies, and the specific cell of origin dictate cancer initiation and propagation across different tissues.

topics.label: Role of the microenvironment and inflammation in tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic inflammatory cues, microenvironmental promoters, and supportive stroma permit and sustain tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for investigating tumor evolution and spatial biology
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the experimental, computational, and spatial profiling technologies used to map cancer cell evolution and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Multi-factorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates how mutational accumulation, cell-of-origin properties, and permissive microenvironmental conditions converge to enable malignancy.

topics.label: Conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the lecture's closing remarks and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapy.
